sourceEvidence.text: Ball for a round object has a Germanic history, possibly through an unattested Old English form or a related Norse word. Ball for a formal dancing party came through French dance vocabulary. The two common meanings share their modern spelling but should not be taught as if a dancing party was named after a round toy.
